correctness.rationale: The unclipped state matrix has characteristic polynomial \(z^2-(1+\beta-q)z+\beta\), so Jury gives local asymptotic stability exactly for \(0<q<2(1+\beta)\). On any nonzero two-cycle, periodicity forces opposite velocities and hence clipped gradients of equal and opposite magnitude \(G=(1+\beta)(a-b)/\alpha\). Scalar clipping leaves only two exhaustive branches: \(G<C\), where both positions are unsaturated and the equations force the critical equality; or \(G=C\), where both are saturated and the gap is \(\alpha C/(1+\beta)\), giving precisely the supercritical center band. In the strictly saturated alternating region the forcing is locally constant, so the velocity perturbation obeys \(e_t=\beta e_{t-1}\) and the center converges along the neutral cycle manifold. Fresh exact rational checks reproduced both critical and supercritical branches; the frozen verifier was independently read.
correctness.risk: The theorem classifies period two and local normal attraction only, not all global recurrent behavior.

value.rationale: The theorem separates bounded oscillation from convergence in a widely used clipped-momentum mechanism and gives a complete, sharp period-two bifurcation with an exact neutral manifold and transverse rate. The result is materially stronger than merely observing one oscillatory example.
value.risk: It is a one-dimensional benchmark and should not be extrapolated to norm clipping in multiple dimensions.

final_claim: For scalar gradient-clipped heavy-ball on \(f(x)=\lambda x^2/2\), clipping the current gradient before raw momentum leaves the local origin-stability threshold at \(\alpha\lambda=2(1+\beta)\); at the threshold all symmetric amplitudes up to the clipping radius are period-two cycles, and above it all nonzero period-two cycles form the stated saturated center band, whose interior is normally attracting with transverse factor \(\beta\).
limitations: No global basin or classification of periods beyond two.
